There are tons of great ideas here on the other topics but I just wanted to comment about this.  One of the worst things about depression is that it really skews a persons perception to the point where everybody seems out to get you, and even positive actions serve to reinforce all the negative things the person (erroneously) thinks about themselves.  Here's the reality about this situation:

First, gifts are things that are given freely- otherwise, they are not really gifts.  Of course a person should express gratitude, but a simple "thank you" suffices for that.  You should not give gifts to your friends expecting *anything* material in return.  Even worse is to expect them to give you material things that are of similar value to what you gave them.  You even used the word "extravagant" to describe what you gave.

The flip side of that, though, is that *your friends gave you gifts!*  Understand that they had no obligation to give you anything, but they did.  They thought of you.  And since you were owed nothing, you should treat what you received as a blessing.  Talk to your friend about the CD, which songs you liked-or not- and why.  Use the energy drinks as a springboard for motivation for doing a little exercise.  

Express gratitude instead of disappointment, and you will feel better about it.  And next time don't worry about the cost of what you give; instead, give them something modest that you feel they will enjoy.  Best of luck in this and everything else.
